text:
For 808 games Boone Jenner was a Blue Jacket. Now, at 33, he is a Washington Capital, and the early returns look a lot like the old Jenner: 8 goals and 12 points in 22 games, 34 hits, 20 blocked shots, 15.6 minutes a night. His scoring rate sits exactly at league average.

The goals run a little ahead of the chances (8 on 5.5 expected, a 16.7% shooting rate against 12.8% for our estimate of his true rate), but the Capitals have scored 3.8 fewer goals than expected with him on the ice, so his linemates are under-finishing even as he converts. Washington gets 53% of the 5v5 expected goals when he plays.

The team around him is the worry. The Capitals lost five straight before beating Philadelphia on Nov. 25, when Jenner had a goal and an assist. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 62% of his shots coming off the rush last season and only 25% of his entries as carries, so his line wins by forechecking and attacking in transition. Evolving-Hockey had him driving play at the 89th percentile. That should travel.
headline: Jenner's first season outside Columbus
